title: Taking away

parent.learn: Taking away means some go away; count what is left.
parent.why: 5 birds, 2 fly off — the birds still sitting are the answer. The sign − means “take away”.
For 9 − 3, start at 9 and step back three: 8, 7, 6. It is adding run backwards.
If 9 − 3 = 6, then 6 + 3 should give 9 again. Putting back what left must return to the start.

parent.learn: Taking away 0 changes nothing; taking away all leaves 0.
parent.why: If nobody leaves, the group stays the same. If everyone leaves, nobody is left: 0.

ask: You have 5 grapes. Eat 2. How many left?
Hold up 6 fingers, fold down 1. How many still up?
There are 4 people in the room. 1 goes out. How many now?
If you have 3 biscuits and eat all of them, how many are left?
Make up a taking-away story with your toys.

rounds.t: There were 3 biscuits. One was eaten. How many are left?
5 birds. 2 flew away. How many are left?

rounds.h: Take all 3 away and nothing is left: 0.

rounds.t: 5 balloons. 1 popped. How many are left?
8 laddoos on a plate. You eat 2. How many are left?

rounds.h: 15 is 1 ten and 5 ones. Take away the 5 ones and 1 ten is left: 10.
First take 2 to reach 10, then 2 more: 8.

rounds.t: 20 pencils in a box. 10 are given away. How many are left?
rounds.h: 2 tens take away 1 ten leaves 1 ten: 10.
